# Use floor-plan-layout

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Lay out a schematic floor plan from a space programme and a footprint, and draw it as a dimensioned SVG — rooms placed as rectangles at real sizes, doors and windows on real walls, overall dimensions, a scale bar and north arrow — with a script that fails the plan when rooms overlap, a room spills outside the footprint, a door sits on no shared wall or a room can't be reached from the entrance.

**Reach for it when** an architect asks to "draw a floor plan", "lay out these rooms", "make a plan for a 10 × 9 m footprint", for a concept plan, a test fit, a zoning diagram or a dimensioned layout from room sizes.

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install floor-plan-layout                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install floor-plan-layout --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install floor-plan-layout --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the Civil architect pack: [`--pack civil-architect`](../packs/use-the-civil-architect-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

It ships scripts, so it needs Python 3 (standard library only, nothing to install). What they may touch is declared in [its manifest](../../../packs/civil-architect/skills/floor-plan-layout/manifest.json).

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "Draw a floor plan for these rooms in a 12 × 15 m footprint"
- "Lay out a 3BHK in this footprint and give me a dimensioned plan"
- "Can you do a quick test fit of the clinic programme on the ground floor?"
- "Make a zoning diagram for the house with the bedrooms away from the road"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Make a Figma diagram of our microservices"
- "Draw a sequence diagram of the checkout flow"
- "Build an interactive diagram of our data pipeline I can click through"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use floor-plan-layout".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **The checker exits 0.** No plan with an overlap, a room outside the outline, a door on no wall or an unreachable room is shown to the user.
- **Every room from the programme is on the plan,** at its target area within 10 %, or the difference is explained.
- **Every stated adjacency is a shared wall,** and every `apart` has a room between.
- **Every habitable room has a window on an outside wall.**
- **No bedroom or living space is reached only through a bathroom, toilet or another bedroom.**
- **The drawing has overall dimensions, room sizes, a scale bar and a north arrow,** and says it is schematic.

- [ground floor](../../../packs/civil-architect/skills/floor-plan-layout/examples/ground-floor.md)

## Use something else when

- Working out the room list and areas from a brief, before any layout: total them first, then plan
- How big the footprint may be under setbacks, coverage and FAR: that is a site feasibility check, done before the plan
- Construction, working or submission drawings in CAD/BIM: this is a schematic for discussion
- Structural grids, MEP routing or a code compliance check
